describe RingBuffer do
  it "starts empty with size 0" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(4)
    rb.empty?.should be_true
    rb.full?.should be_false
    rb.size.should eq 0
  end

  it "tracks size correctly after pushes" do
    rb = RingBuffer(String).new(3)
    rb.push("a")
    rb.size.should eq 1
    rb.push("b")
    rb.size.should eq 2
    rb.push("c")
    rb.size.should eq 3
    rb.full?.should be_true
    rb.empty?.should be_false
  end

  it "pops elements in FIFO order" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(3)
    rb.push(10)
    rb.push(20)
    rb.push(30)
    rb.pop.should eq 10
    rb.pop.should eq 20
    rb.pop.should eq 30
  end

  it "raises IndexError when popping from an empty buffer" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(2)
    expect_raises(IndexError, "buffer is empty") { rb.pop }
  end

  it "overwrites the oldest element when pushing to a full buffer" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(3)
    rb.push(1).push(2).push(3)
    rb.full?.should be_true
    rb.push(4) # overwrites 1
    rb.size.should eq 3
    rb.full?.should be_true
    rb.pop.should eq 2
    rb.pop.should eq 3
    rb.pop.should eq 4
  end

  it "maintains correct size after overwrite" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(2)
    rb.push(1).push(2)
    rb.push(3) # overwrites 1, size stays 2
    rb.size.should eq 2
  end

  it "supports push chaining (returns self)" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(5)
    result = rb.push(1).push(2).push(3)
    result.should be(rb)
    rb.size.should eq 3
  end

  it "correctly handles a capacity-1 buffer" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(1)
    rb.push(42)
    rb.full?.should be_true
    rb.push(99) # overwrites 42
    rb.pop.should eq 99
    rb.empty?.should be_true
  end

  it "correctly wraps around the ring multiple times" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(3)
    (1..9).each { |i| rb.push(i) }
    # After 9 pushes into capacity-3, last 3 pushed are 7, 8, 9
    rb.pop.should eq 7
    rb.pop.should eq 8
    rb.pop.should eq 9
  end

  it "works with a String generic type" do
    rb = RingBuffer(String).new(2)
    rb.push("hello").push("world")
    rb.pop.should eq "hello"
    rb.pop.should eq "world"
    rb.empty?.should be_true
  end

  it "interleaves push and pop correctly" do
    rb = RingBuffer(Int32).new(3)
    rb.push(1).push(2)
    rb.pop.should eq 1
    rb.push(3).push(4)
    rb.size.should eq 3
    rb.pop.should eq 2
    rb.pop.should eq 3
    rb.pop.should eq 4
  end
end

abstract class Shape
  abstract def area : Float64

  def larger_than?(other : Shape) : Bool
    area > other.area
  end
end

class Circle < Shape
  def initialize(@radius : Float64)
  end

  def area : Float64
    Math::PI * @radius ** 2
  end
end

class Rectangle < Shape
  def initialize(@width : Float64, @height : Float64)
  end

  def area : Float64

  end

describe Shape do
  describe Circle do
    it "computes area as PI * r^2" do
      c = Circle.new(1.0)
      c.area.should be_close(Math::PI, 1e-9)
    end

    it "computes area for radius 5" do
      c = Circle.new(5.0)
      c.area.should be_close(Math::PI * 25.0, 1e-9)
    end

    it "computes area 0 for radius 0" do
      c = Circle.new(0.0)
      c.area.should be_close(0.0, 1e-9)
    end

    it "is a Shape" do
      Circle.new(1.0).should be_a(Shape)
    end
  end

  describe Rectangle do
    it "computes area as width * height" do
      r = Rectangle.new(4.0, 5.0)
      r.area.should eq 20.0
    end

    it "computes area 0 when one dimension is 0" do
      r = Rectangle.new(0.0, 10.0)
      r.area.should eq 0.0
    end

    it "is a Shape" do
      Rectangle.new(1.0, 2.0).should be_a(Shape)
    end
  end

  describe "#larger_than?" do
    it "returns true when self has a bigger area" do
      big = Circle.new(10.0)
      small = Rectangle.new(1.0, 1.0)
      big.larger_than?(small).should be_true
    end

    it "returns false when self has a smaller area" do
      small = Circle.new(0.5)
      big = Rectangle.new(100.0, 100.0)
      small.larger_than?(big).should be_false
    end

    it "returns false when areas are equal" do
      r1 = Rectangle.new(2.0, 3.0)
      r2 = Rectangle.new(6.0, 1.0)
      r1.larger_than?(r2).should be_false
      r2.larger_than?(r1).should be_false
    end

    it "compares cross-type shapes correctly" do
      c = Circle.new(3.0)     # ~28.27
      r = Rectangle.new(5.0, 5.0) # 25.0
      c.larger_than?(r).should be_true
      r.larger_than?(c).should be_false
    end

    it "is not commutative when areas differ" do
      a = Rectangle.new(3.0, 4.0) # 12
      b = Rectangle.new(2.0, 5.0) # 10
      a.larger_than?(b).should be_true
      b.larger_than?(a).should be_false
    end
  end
end

Write a crystal spec for the following code. Use describe/it with concrete assertions and cover edge cases.

struct Vector2D
  getter x : Float64
  getter y : Float64

  def initialize(@x : Float64, @y : Float64)
  end

  def +(other : Vector2D) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x + other.x, @y + other.y)
  end

  def -(other : Vector2D) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x - other.x, @y - other.y)
  end

  def *(scalar : Float64) : Vector2D
    Vector2D.new(@x * scalar, @y * scalar)
  end

  def magnitude : Float64
    Math.sqrt(@x ** 2 + @y ** 2)
  end

  def normalize : Vector2D
    m = magnitude
    raise ArgumentError.new("cannot normalize a zero vector") if m == 0.0
    Vector2D.new(@x / m, @y / m)
  end

  def ==(other : Vector2D) : Bool
    @x == other.x && @y == other.y
  end
end

describe InventoryLedger do
  it "returns 0 for an unseen SKU" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.stock_for("WIDGET-A").should eq 0
  end

  it "is unavailable for unseen SKUs" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.available?("NEW-SKU").should be_false
  end

  it "tracks stock after a positive adjustment" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("SKU-1", 50)
    ledger.stock_for("SKU-1").should eq 50
    ledger.available?("SKU-1").should be_true
  end

  it "accumulates multiple adjustments for the same SKU" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("SKU-1", 100)
    ledger.adjust("SKU-1", -30)
    ledger.adjust("SKU-1", 10)
    ledger.stock_for("SKU-1").should eq 80
  end

  it "returns self from adjust for chaining" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    result = ledger.adjust("A", 5).adjust("B", 10)
    result.should be(ledger)
    ledger.stock_for("A").should eq 5
    ledger.stock_for("B").should eq 10
  end

  it "marks SKU as unavailable when stock reaches 0" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("SKU-X", 5)
    ledger.adjust("SKU-X", -5)
    ledger.available?("SKU-X").should be_false
    ledger.stock_for("SKU-X").should eq 0
  end

  it "allows negative stock via adjustment" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("SKU-BACK", -10)
    ledger.stock_for("SKU-BACK").should eq -10
    ledger.available?("SKU-BACK").should be_false
  end

  it "low_stock returns SKUs at or below threshold" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("A", 5)
    ledger.adjust("B", 10)
    ledger.adjust("C", 2)
    low = ledger.low_stock(5)
    low.should contain("A")
    low.should contain("C")
    low.should_not contain("B")
  end

  it "low_stock threshold 0 returns only zero-stock SKUs" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("OUT", 0)
    ledger.adjust("IN", 1)
    ledger.low_stock(0).should contain("OUT")
    ledger.low_stock(0).should_not contain("IN")
  end

  it "low_stock returns empty array when nothing is low" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("A", 100)
    ledger.adjust("B", 200)
    ledger.low_stock(5).should be_empty
  end

  it "handles multiple independent SKUs independently" do
    ledger = InventoryLedger.new
    ledger.adjust("X", 3)
    ledger.adjust("Y", 7)
    ledger.stock_for("X").should eq 3
    ledger.stock_for("Y").should eq 7
  end
end

describe "midpoint" do
  it "returns the midpoint between two points on the x-axis" do
    a = {x: 0.0, y: 0.0, z: 0.0}

    result[:z].should eq(-4.0)

    result[:x].should eq(-4.0)
    result[:y].should eq(-6.0)
    result[:z].should eq(-8.0)

    r.includes?("rust").should be_true
    r.includes?("c").should be_true

    r.size.should eq 1

    r1 = TagRegistry.new.add_all(["a", "b", "c"])

    r1 = TagRegistry.new.add("a")
    r2 = TagRegistry.new.add("b")

  end

  it "exclusive_to returns tags in self but not in other" do

    excl = r1.exclusive_to(r2)

  end

  it "exclusive_to returns all self tags when other is empty" do
    r1 = TagRegistry.new.add_all(["x", "y"])
    r2 = TagRegistry.new

    combined.should eq Set{"a", "b", "c"}

    r2 = TagRegistry.new.add("only-in-r2")
    r1.combined_with(r2)
    r1.size.should eq 1
    r2.size.should eq 1
  end

class Pipeline
  def run(n : Int32) : Array(Int32)
    channel = Channel(Int32).new(capacity: 16)
    results = [] of Int32

    result = fc.top(1)
    result.size.should eq 1
    result[0][:item].should eq "common"
    result[0][:count].should eq 5
  end

  end

class ConfigLoader
  class ParseError < Exception
    getter line_number : Int32
    getter raw_line : String

    def initialize(@line_number : Int32, @raw_line : String)
      super("Parse error on line #{@line_number}: #{@raw_line.inspect}")
    end
  end

  def self.load(path : String) : Hash(String, String)
    result = {} of String => String
    file = File.open(path)
    begin
      file.each_line.with_index(1) do |line, lineno|
        stripped = line.strip
        next if stripped.empty? || stripped.starts_with?('#')
        eq = stripped.index('=')
        raise ParseError.new(lineno, line) unless eq
        key = stripped[0...eq].strip
        raise ParseError.new(lineno, line) if key.empty?
        result[key] = stripped[(eq + 1)..].strip
      end
    ensure
      file.close
    end
    result
  end
end

require "file"

module IniConfig
  def self.load(path : String) : Hash(String, Hash(String, String))
    result = Hash(String, Hash(String, String)).new
    section = "default"
    result[section] = Hash(String, String).new

    File.open(path) do |f|
      f.each_line do |raw|
        line = raw.strip
        next if line.empty? || line.starts_with?(';') || line.starts_with?('#')

        if line.starts_with?('[') && line.ends_with?(']')
          section = line[1..-2].strip
          result[section] ||= Hash(String, String).new
        elsif (eq = line.index('='))
          key = line[0...eq].strip
          value = line[(eq + 1)..].strip
          result[section][key] = value
        end
      end
    end

    result
  end
end

require "io/memory"
require "file"

class MemoryReport
  def initialize
    @sections = [] of {String, String}
  end

  def add_section(name : String, body : String) : Nil
    @sections << {name, body}
  end

  def save(path : String) : Nil
    buf = IO::Memory.new
    @sections.each_with_index do |(name, body), i|
      buf << "=== " << name << " ===\n"
      buf << body
      buf << "\n" unless body.ends_with?('\n')
      buf << "\n" if i < @sections.size - 1
    end
    File.write(path, buf.to_s)
  end
end

class TokenScanner
  TOKEN_PATTERNS = [
    {:number, /\A\d+/},
    {:word, /\A[a-zA-Z]+/},
    {:symbol, /\A\S/},
  ]

  def initialize(source : String)
    @source = source
    @pos = 0
  end

  def next_token : NamedTuple(kind: Symbol, value: String)?
    skip_whitespace
    return nil if @pos >= @source.size

    remaining = @source[@pos..]
    TOKEN_PATTERNS.each do |kind, pattern|
      if m = remaining.match(pattern)
        @pos += m[0].size
        return {kind: kind, value: m[0]}
      end
    end

    nil
  end

  def tokens : Array(NamedTuple(kind: Symbol, value: String))
    result = [] of NamedTuple(kind: Symbol, value: String)
    while tok = next_token
      result << tok
    end
    result
  end

  private def skip_whitespace : Nil
    while @pos < @source.size && @source[@pos].ascii_whitespace?
      @pos += 1
    end
  end
end

def format_duration(span : Time::Span) : String
  prefix = span.negative? ? "-" : ""
  span = span.abs

  hours = total_s // 3600
  minutes = (total_s % 3600) // 60
  seconds = total_s % 60

  elsif minutes > 0

  else
    "#{seconds}s"
  end

  prefix + body
end

class RateLimiter
  def initialize(@limit : Int32, @window : Time::Span)
    @events = Deque(Time::Instant).new
  end

  def allow? : Bool
    now = Time.instant
    purge_old(now)
    if @events.size < @limit
      @events << now
      true
    else
      false
    end
  end

  def remaining : Int32
    purge_old(Time.instant)
    (@limit - @events.size).clamp(0, @limit)
  end

  private def purge_old(now : Time::Instant) : Nil
    cutoff = now - @window
    while !@events.empty? && @events.first < cutoff
      @events.shift
    end
  end
end

describe RateLimiter do
  it "allows events up to the limit" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(3, 1.minute)
    rl.allow?.should be_true
    rl.allow?.should be_true
    rl.allow?.should be_true
  end

  it "denies the event that exceeds the limit" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(2, 1.minute)
    rl.allow?
    rl.allow?
    rl.allow?.should be_false
  end

  it "remaining starts at the full limit" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(5, 1.minute)
    rl.remaining.should eq 5
  end

  it "remaining decrements with each allowed event" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(5, 1.minute)
    rl.allow?
    rl.remaining.should eq 4
    rl.allow?
    rl.remaining.should eq 3
  end

  it "remaining is zero when at the limit" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(2, 1.minute)
    rl.allow?
    rl.allow?
    rl.remaining.should eq 0
  end

  it "remaining does not go below zero" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(1, 1.minute)
    rl.allow?
    rl.allow?  # denied
    rl.remaining.should eq 0
  end

  it "limit of 1 allows exactly one event then denies" do
    rl = RateLimiter.new(1, 1.minute)
    rl.allow?.should be_true
    rl.allow?.should be_false
  end

  it "with a very small window, old events are evicted and new ones are allowed" do
    # Use a 1-nanosecond window so any events from a prior call expire immediately
    rl = RateLimiter.new(1, Time::Span.new(nanoseconds: 1))
    rl.allow?.should be_true
    # Sleep long enough to expire (at least 1 ms to be safe with OS scheduling)
    sleep 1.millisecond
    rl.allow?.should be_true
  end
end

Write a crystal spec for the following code. Use describe/it with concrete assertions and cover edge cases.

class DeadlineTracker
  def initialize(@deadline : Time)
  end

  def expired? : Bool
    Time.utc >= @deadline
  end

  def time_remaining : Time::Span
    remaining = @deadline - Time.utc
    remaining.negative? ? Time::Span.zero : remaining
  end

  def urgency : Symbol
    remaining = time_remaining
    if remaining <= 10.minutes
      :critical
    elsif remaining <= 1.hour
      :warning
    else
      :ok
    end
  end
end

describe DeadlineTracker do
  it "is not expired when deadline is in the future" do
    tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 1.hour)
    tracker.expired?.should be_false
  end

  it "is expired when deadline is in the past" do
    tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc - 1.second)
    tracker.expired?.should be_true
  end

  it "is expired when deadline is exactly now (or just passed)" do
    # Use a deadline 1 ms in the past to reliably test the >= boundary
    tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc - 1.millisecond)
    tracker.expired?.should be_true
  end

  describe "time_remaining" do
    it "returns a positive span when not expired" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 2.hours)
      tracker.time_remaining.should be > Time::Span.zero
    end

    it "returns Time::Span.zero when expired" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc - 1.hour)
      tracker.time_remaining.should eq Time::Span.zero
    end

    it "never returns a negative span" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc - 10.minutes)
      tracker.time_remaining.should be >= Time::Span.zero
    end
  end

  describe "urgency" do
    it "returns :ok when more than 1 hour remains" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 2.hours)
      tracker.urgency.should eq :ok
    end

    it "returns :warning when between 10 minutes and 1 hour remain" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 30.minutes)
      tracker.urgency.should eq :warning
    end

    it "returns :critical when 10 minutes or less remain" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 5.minutes)
      tracker.urgency.should eq :critical
    end

    it "returns :critical when already expired" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc - 1.minute)
      tracker.urgency.should eq :critical
    end

    it "returns :critical exactly at the 10-minute boundary" do
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 10.minutes)
      tracker.urgency.should eq :critical
    end

    it "returns :warning exactly at the 1-hour boundary" do
      # Just under 1 hour: 59m 59s
      tracker = DeadlineTracker.new(Time.utc + 59.minutes + 59.seconds)
      tracker.urgency.should eq :warning
    end
  end
end
